candidate: A — Treasury duration carry via yield-curve steepness + roll-down, long/flat only, no naked short
mechanism: curve steepness (e.g. DGS10-DGS2) adjusts duration exposure across a short/mid/long Treasury-ETF ladder to earn yield + roll-down
data_policy: free sources only, no paid deps, no API key; TrdEnv.SIMULATE hard-lock; anti-look-ahead; killer window 2022 rate shock must be covered.
preregistration_note: signal prereg is 营缮's to freeze (CARRY_EVAL_PREREGISTRATION.md template; signal written from zero — repo carry_* is EVO-25 VIX term-structure carry, a DIFFERENT premium family, NOT reused). The universe substitution below was decided BEFORE prereg freeze (data availability, not post-hoc tuning) and its rationale must be written into the prereg.

universe.substitution: SHY (1-3y) is unavailable — see treasury_etf_bars.archived_blocker (free equity sources IP-block this egress; OpenD gateway down). BIL (1-3mo T-bills) takes the short-duration / cash-avoidance leg. A's mechanism needs three duration points (short/mid/long); BIL fills the short point (GEM also used BIL as its cash leg). Decided pre-freeze by 工部尚书 (2026-07-29), flagged for 都察院 review; reversible while prereg is unfrozen.
universe.substitution_bias_2022: IMPORTANT — the substitution is FAVORABLE to A's 2022 killer test and must be declared as such in the report: BIL (1-3mo, duration ~0) was materially more resilient in 2022 than SHY (1-3y, duration ~1.9): BIL ~+1.5% vs SHY ~-3.5% over the year. Because A's `slope<0 -> short leg` rule sends the book to the short leg exactly in the 2022 inversion, using BIL instead of SHY makes the 2022 result BETTER than the original SHY spec would have. So A's 2022 outcome must be read as an UPPER BOUND relative to the SHY spec, not a like-for-like — the report must state this so the substitution does not silently flatter the candidate.

yield_curve.source: FRED H.15 constant-maturity (fredgraph.csv, no API key)
yield_curve.units: percent per annum, close-of-day constant maturity
yield_curve.missing_policy: FRED '.' markers dropped, never forward-filled (no synthetic values)
yield_curve.look_ahead_note: H.15 is close-of-day for the trade date; decide at close t, execute t+1 open -> look-ahead-free. Consumer owns any lag.
yield_curve.refetch_command: python -c "from qlab.events.datafetch.fred_yields import fetch_curve, write_parquet; w,n=fetch_curve(start='2002-01-01', end='2026-12-31'); write_parquet(w,'data/fred_yields.parquet'); print(n)"

treasury_etf_bars.status: DELIVERED (committed) — gathered from existing in-repo bars on sibling branches; no new fetch, no external egress needed
treasury_etf_bars.layout: data/rate_carry/{SYM}_1d.parquet, columns [date,open,high,low,close,volume]; same contract as ParquetDailyBarSource
treasury_etf_bars.adjustment_basis: split + DIVIDEND adjusted (total return). Verified: a price-only bond-ETF series would drift to ~0 CAGR over this rate cycle; here IEF +3.44% / TLT +3.27% / BIL +1.37% (~avg short rate) are total-return-consistent, and TLT's 2006-07-03 close is 44.35 vs its actual ~88 listing price — i.e. ~19y of coupons back-adjusted in. Dividend adjustment is mandatory for bond ETFs (coupons are ~all of the return).
treasury_etf_bars.original_bar_source: moomoo OpenD K_DAY qfq (forward-adjusted, dividend+split) — the same total-return source as data/daily_full
